prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures a steep downward egocentric view in a workshop space, showing the camera wearer's upper torso (~0.2–0.4 m away) at the bottom and their arms extending forward (~0.4–0.8 m) above a brown drop-cloth floor (~1.5–1.8 m below head height). Across frames 1 to 5, as the wearer sets down a yellow circular saw on a wooden worktable (~0.7–1.0 m in front in frames 1–2) and turns left while walking forward across the room, the elevated table surface, the handheld wooden trim piece (~0.5–0.8 m), and a green A-frame ladder (~0.8–1.4 m to the left in frames 1–2, then front-right in frames 3–5) stand out as mid-bright structures above the dark floor plane and a round shop vacuum (~1.2–1.5 m away on the floor). Compared to the RGB strip alone, the depth gradient makes the vertical height differences between the raised tabletop, the ladder steps, the low sawhorses on the left (~1.2–1.6 m away in frames 3–5), and the ground immediately clear despite the flat overhead lighting and cluttered textures. In frame 5, a second person crouching on the floor in a blue shirt ~2.2–2.5 m ahead (and ~1.5 m beyond the ladder and a small white box) appears only as a faint dark silhouette near the top edge, with their head partly cropped out of view and facing away from the camera wearer. The depth map is unreliable along the right window frame in frame 1 (where it drops to pure black), blurs the thin handheld wooden trim into the dark floor in frames 2–3, and flattens the crouching person in frame 5 into the surrounding floor depth.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the camera wearer's torso, legs, and outstretched arms in the lower foreground (~0.2–0.8 m from the camera) across all five frames as the wearer turns left away from the worktable (frames 1–2) and walks across the drop cloth while passing a wooden trim piece from the left hand (frames 1–3) to the right hand (frames 4–5). In frame 5, it detects the second person crouching on the floor at the top-center (~2.2–2.5 m in front of the wearer and ~0.8 m behind a white box to their left), whose back is turned and head is occluded by the top frame border so they do not look toward the camera wearer. While the segmentation masks sharply delineate the outer boundary of the wearer's body and arms against the cluttered background—separating the wearer's reach envelope from the table and floor more cleanly than RGB—the map fails to segment nearly all workshop objects, including the worktable, circular saw, green ladder, shop vacuum, and sawhorses. Furthermore, the labels and instance splits are highly unreliable: frames 1 and 2 split the camera wearer's own body and right arm/saw into two overlapping 'person' instances, frame 3 mislabels the green ladder side-rail (~1.2 m away at top-center) as a 'toothbrush', and frame 5 misclassifies the wearer's right foot (~1.5 m below) as a 'cell phone' and the wooden trim held in the right hand (~0.6 m away) as a 'remote'.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost completely blank across the five-frame sequence, detecting only three isolated magenta hand skeletons within arm's reach (~0.5–0.7 m in front of and below the camera) and failing to render any yellow body keypoints for either the camera wearer or the second person crouching ~2.2–2.5 m ahead in frame 5. Specifically, it localizes the wearer's right hand gripping the circular saw handle over the worktable in frame 1 (~0.5 m front-right), the left hand holding the wooden board at the lower-left edge in frame 2 (~0.6 m front-left, partly cropped by the frame border), and the right hand curled at the wearer's side in frame 3 (~0.6 m front-right) as the wearer turns and walks forward. Where present, these magenta wireframes reveal the exact finger articulation and grip orientation on the saw and wood more explicitly than the motion-blurred RGB frames. However, the map is largely unreliable for broader spatial understanding due to severe top-down self-occlusion of the wearer's head and shoulders and the cropping of the distant crouching person, missing the wearer's left hand in frames 1 and 3, the right hand on the saw in frame 2, and all body and hand poses throughout frames 4 and 5.
